note: Scripture authority is the 1962 Amharic Bible (UBS; NT revised 2003). Its New Testament is on disk whole (ebible mirror gracious-tech/fetch_collection, bibles/amh_amh; re-verified for this job 2026-10-08: all 27 NT books return 200 as usfm/, gen/psa/isa 404, no usx/). The mirror carries no Old Testament, so OT quotations reuse the wording of an already-shipped Amharic work where one quotes the same verse (source_file names it) and are otherwise self_rendered in the 1962 register.

A `mined` row was re-measured against the finished text: an exact substring of at least 20 characters of the 1962 NT verse (or 25 of the cited corpus file) inside that block. Shorter, re-personed or partly composed quotations are self_rendered, whatever the translator believed.

The English epigraphs are simplified child paraphrases ("— from Psalm 139"); per the shipped am children's editions each quotes the 1962 Bible's own wording for the part the English means, with … for words left out, and cites `— ከ<Book> <chapter>`. Where the teen am edition (samuel-ajayi-crowther-a-life-teens) already rendered a verse, its wording is reused verbatim so the two editions agree: Psalm 10:14 and 1 Samuel 2:8 are the teen's self_rendered wording and stay self_rendered here; Psalm 4:8 matches rooted-4.am.json and 1 Samuel 3:18 matches essentials-of-prayer.am.json. Psalm 139:16 reuses one clause of rooted-6.am.json but composes the rest, so it is self_rendered. Psalm 124:7 and 1 Kings 17:6 have no shipped Amharic rendering and are self_rendered. Chapter 8's prayer opens with the 1962 wording of Matthew 6:9 because the English prayer itself opens "Our Father in heaven".
